title: Add feature flag gates for route experiments (beta enablement + rollback)
author: Hannah Rivera
release_notes: Route-level experiments are now gated behind a feature flag with account allowlisting for beta and an emergency kill switch for safe rollback.
body: Summary: Introduces first-class feature flag gates for Route-level A/B testing (“route experiments”) across the control plane and data plane so we can: (1) enable beta accounts safely (allowlist), (2) do region-by-region rollout, and (3) have a single kill switch for emergency rollback. This PR does not change experiment semantics; it only gates evaluation + API surfacing. Context/why: As we expand beta (Phase 2) we need a deterministic, auditable enablement mechanism that does not require config churn or code deploys. We also want to avoid partial enablement (Console shows experiments but router ignores them, or vice versa). This PR aligns gating across: policy engine evaluator, router request context, and Console APIs. Rollout plan references: ENG-9036 release train plan + internal thread “feature-flag plan for beta enablement” (eng-releases/1736700299). What’s included: (1) New flags: ff.route_experiments.enabled (global per-env; defaults false outside staging), ff.route_experiments.allowlist_org_ids (comma-separated org ids for beta), ff.route_experiments.debug_headers (controls returning x-redwood-experiment-* headers), ff.route_experiments.kill_switch (hard off regardless of other settings). (2) Centralized gate function in policy engine: shouldEvaluateRouteExperiments(ctx) which checks env + org allowlist + kill switch and emits a single structured log line and a metric. (3) Router integration: if gated off, do not evaluate experiment assignment; omit experiment_id/variant_id from request context to prevent partial attribution. (4) Console API integration: experiment create/start/stop endpoints return 403 FeatureNotEnabled for orgs not allowlisted; list/detail endpoints hide the “Experiments” surfaces (returns empty list) for non-enabled orgs (keeps UI simple for GA later). (5) Telemetry: emits counter redwood.route_experiments.gate_decision{decision=enabled|disabled,reason=env|allowlist|kill_switch} to help us validate rollout and catch misconfig. (6) Docs/comments: inline notes and a short ops note pointing to the beta enablement runbook (to be added in the SRE doc set). Guardrails: We explicitly treat the kill switch as highest priority; it is intended for incident response and can be flipped without deploy. We also default debug_headers to false for beta to reduce customer confusion until docs/tooltips ship (tracked separately). Test plan: Unit tests cover gate precedence (kill switch wins), allowlist parsing, and consistent behavior across evaluator + Console API guard. Integration test updated to assert that when the flag is off, assignment is bypassed and attribution dimensions are not emitted. Manual: in staging, enable org allowlist for INT-1193 beta account and verify Console can create experiment and router returns x-redwood-experiment-variant only when debug_headers is enabled. Notes/risks: This introduces config-driven behavior; if config service is stale, we prefer “off” (safe default) and emit gate_decision{reason=stale_config} (added here) rather than attempting best-effort enablement. Follow-ups: (a) move allowlist to first-class Experiment Service entitlement table (post-beta), (b) Console UI gating for nav item (currently API-gated), (c) add runbook steps for toggling kill switch + comms template (SRE-owned).
commits: feat(flags): add ff.route_experiments.* config keys and helpers
feat(policy-engine): gate experiment evaluator behind feature flag + kill switch
feat(router): bypass experiment assignment + attribution when gated off
feat(console-api): enforce FeatureNotEnabled for experiment mutation endpoints
obs: emit gate decision metric + structured log fields
test: add unit tests for allowlist parsing and precedence
chore: rename internal headers behind debug_headers flag
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (request changes): Can we ensure cross-region config staleness defaults to OFF? We don’t want one region evaluating experiments while another doesn’t due to cached config. Also please make the reason dimension explicit so dashboards can distinguish allowlist vs kill switch. Hannah Rivera (author): Agreed. Updated gate to treat missing/expired config as disabled, added reason=stale_config, and ensured the same gate function is used from both router and evaluator paths. Pushed commit 4c12a77. Sean Gallagher: +1 on safe default. Please add a metric for gate decisions; we’ll need it for rollout checkpoints. Also ensure kill switch is a single knob (no need to edit allowlists during incident). Hannah Rivera: Added redwood.route_experiments.gate_decision with decision/reason labels; kill switch is checked first and overrides allowlist/env. Marcus Lin: For Console API, returning 403 with a generic message is fine, but avoid leaking allowlist details in error text. Also verify debug endpoint/header flag is internal-only. Hannah Rivera: Updated error response to "feature_not_enabled" without allowlist hints; debug_headers defaults false and requires config access. Dylan Brooks: Looks good. One nit: name the flags consistently with other rollouts flags (ff.rollouts.* vs ff.route_experiments.*). Hannah Rivera: Kept ff.route_experiments.* per release plan, but added alias parsing for ff.rollouts.route_experiments_enabled for internal compatibility; left a TODO to remove alias at GA. Connor O'Brien: Approved; this matches the staged beta enablement plan. Please link this PR in the release checklist ticket. Hannah Rivera: Linked in ENG-9036 and added rollout note in the ticket.
